text: Fully Funded 3-slide carousel. Slide 1: 'Rich Habits, Decoded · No. 1' badge, then 'Paid Friday. Broke by Wednesday?' in a large serif with highlighted words, the handwritten note 'new one every Mon · Wed · Fri' and a small drawn chart, 'paycheque left', with bars shrinking from Friday to an empty Wednesday. Slide 2: Pay yourself first. (move it the day it lands). Slide 3: Then raise it with every raise. (In one study, workers who did went from saving 3.5% to 13.6%.) Source: Thaler & Benartzi, 2004.

Littlefold 2-slide carousel. Slide 1: '3 am Club · No. 1' badge, 'It's 3 am. You're feeding. Eyes closing.' in a large serif with highlighted words, a halftone baby shoe, and the handwritten note 'new night tip every Mon · Wed · Fri'. Slide 2: 'Sleepy? Don't feed on the sofa or armchair.' Handwritten: after the feed, baby back in their own crib, on their back. Source: NHS, The Lullaby Trust.

Locked Hour 3-slide carousel. Slide 1: black label 'One Word · No. 2', the line 'Inbox open all day again?' and the huge word 'Batch.' over a pink highlighter stripe, with a halftone alarm clock and the note '3 email checks a day, not all day'. Slide 2: '3 checks. That's it.' A clock ring with pink marks at 9:30, 1:00 and 4:30; 'Tab closed in between. Urgent? People can call or text.' Slide 3: 'Less stress.' In a 2-week study, the week people checked email 3 times a day felt calmer than the week they checked whenever. Do this: write your 3 check times on a sticky note. Close the tab. Source: Kushlev & Dunn 2015.

Hourback 3-slide carousel. Slide 1: 'AI's answer felt generic again?' in a large serif with highlighted words, black-and-white chat bubbles, and the handwritten note 'new one every Mon · Wed · Fri'. Slide 2: Before you answer, ask me 3 questions. (add this line to any request). Slide 3: What it asked me: (real reply, shortened).

Edited video in the Hourback look. Big serif "Stranger in your best photo?" over a drawn phone showing a beach photo of a cat seen from behind, with a stranger in an orange jacket in the background. A yellow finger trail circles the stranger and they dissolve into pixels, leaving clean sand: "circle them. gone." "Your phone's AI erases them," with before and after photos. Then the steps as tapped buttons: "On iPhone: Photos, Edit, Clean Up", "Any phone: Google Photos, Edit, Magic Eraser, Erase". Then "Do this: Photos, Edit, Clean Up, circle them." with "circle them." circled by hand, a small Android line, a send line and a follow line. It loops back to the opening. Drawn for this post.

Illustrated Reel in warm light: pastel sky, sage hills, a smiling sun and a washing line of baby clothes. A baby's arm in a pink sleeve reaches up into the frame; the little hand (no face shown) has sharp nail tips that sparkle, and a soft pink emery board files each tip round. Seen from above, a swaddled baby sleeps on their back in a crib on a flat mattress with nothing else in it, one arm out, while the board gently files a fingertip under a moon; a tooth wobbles and gets a 'no' ring, and an emery board gets a check. Text: scratches on their face again? Keep tiny nails short and smooth. So they can't scratch themselves. / the gentle way: File with a soft emery board. Or use baby nail clippers. / the easy time: While they're asleep. Or after a bath, if they lie still. / and: Don't bite them short. Biting can pass an infection to their finger. / Do this: Tonight: file their nails while they sleep. Send this to someone with a brand-new baby. Follow for one calm thing a night. Source chips: AAP, NHS.

Illustrated Reel in soft morning light: pastel sky, sage hills, a smiling sun and a washing line of tiny baby clothes swaying in the wind. An adult's bent arm dips its elbow into a pink baby bath, ripples spread, the steam settles and a check appears. A blue tap runs first, then a coral tap adds a shimmering, steaming hot patch, and a hand swirls it away. A phone buzzes; adult hands hold a baby wrapped in a hooded towel (no face shown) out of the bath and carry it along. The elbow dips again while a rubber duck bobs, bubbles and hearts float up, and a hooded towel is pegged on the line. Text: Bath water too hot? Dip your elbow in first. It should feel warm, not hot. / filling it? Cold water first. Then hot. Mix it well. So there are no hot patches. / and always: Never leave them alone in the bath. Not for a second. Phone or doorbell? Take baby with you. / Do this: Elbow in. Then baby in. Send this to whoever does bath time. Follow for one calm thing a night. Source chips: NHS, AAP.

Edited video on a blue blueprint grid. A drawn credit card statement: the 'minimum' line is ticked and 'interest $48.50' appears in coral, under 'Paid on time. Still charged interest?'. Then 'Pay the minimum? You pay interest. Pay it all? $0 interest.' with two bars drawn to scale: a coral one labelled '$48.50 interest' and a blue one labelled 'interest-free'. Then 'Do this: Set autopay to full balance.' as the selection on a drawn phone screen moves from 'Minimum' to 'Full balance' and a tick appears. It loops.

Littlefold tile: 'Breastfeeding? 5 signs it's going well' in a large serif above a taped yellow sticky note with ticks: 6+ heavy wet diapers a day (from day 5 after birth); 2+ soft yellow poops a day (from day 4 after birth); long sucks and swallows; lets go of the breast on their own; steady weight gain. A halftone baby shoe, the handwritten note 'do this: count wet diapers for 24 hours', and 'Source: NHS'.

Fully Funded tile, a 'say it differently' card. Instead of: 'It's only $150.' (crossed out). Say: 'That's 8 hours of work.' Line: The maths: $750 take-home a week ÷ 40 hours = $18.75 an hour. Do this: before any buy over $50, divide by your hourly take-home.

Edited video in the Hourback look. Big serif "Kid's fractions. You forgot how?" over a large drawn worksheet: "A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. Sam eats 3 slices and Priya eats 2. What fraction of the pizza is left?" with a drawn pizza and the note "help, without giving the answer". A request types into Claude, an AI chat app: "My kid is in Grade 5 and stuck on this homework question:" then the question, then "Give me 3 short hints I can say out loud, one at a time. Don't give the answer." "AI gives hints, not the answer." Claude's real reply then shows one large hint at a time, with three progress dots, while the pizza acts it out: "8 slices in all", "3 + 2 eaten" with 5 slices greyed, "how many left?" with 3 slices glowing. "Check it: did the answer slip in? Ours didn't. It's 3/8. Let them say it." Then "Do this: Type the question. Add: 'Hints, not the answer.' In ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini." with a send line and a follow line. It loops back to the opening.

Illustrated Reel in soft afternoon light: pastel sky, sage hills, a smiling sun and a washing line of tiny baby clothes. Seen from above on a soft blue mattress, a baby with a green knit hat (no face shown) lies on a thin butter-yellow blanket; the legs bend up and out into a frog shape, the blanket folds over the chest from each side, and the bottom folds up loosely with the bent pink legs visible through it and arrows marked 'room here'. An adult hand and forearm slide two fingers under the wrap at the chest and a check appears. The wrapped baby rocks as if trying to roll, then the swaddle comes off, arms free. The loose-hip wrap returns with hearts, and the blanket hangs on the line. Text: Swaddling? Leave room for the hips. Legs bend up and out. Tight, straight legs can harm their hips. / check the chest: Slide 2 or 3 fingers between the wrap and their chest. If they fit, it's not too tight. / when to stop: Trying to roll? Stop swaddling. Some start trying at 2 months. / Do this: Tonight, leave room at the hips. Send this to whoever does the night feeds. Follow for one calm thing a night. Source chip: AAP.

Edited zine-style video on pink, yellow and cream with a dot grid. A pink highlighter sweeps across an open notebook under 'Exam next week? Stop rereading.' The book snaps shut and a pencil writes lines on a blank page. Then 'Students who wrote it from memory remembered 61%.' with two bars growing, one week later: 'from memory' 61% and 'read 4×' 40%, the numbers in huge type. Then 'Do this: Shut the book. Write what you remember.' with the closed book and the page being written. It loops.

Fully Funded 3-slide carousel. Slide 1: 'Rich Habits, Decoded · No. 2' badge, '$15 lunch, every workday?' in a large serif with highlighted words, the handwritten note 'new one every Mon · Wed · Fri' and a small drawn bar chart, 'lunch money, 1 year': buy 5 days $3,600, pack 3 days $2,016. Slide 2: Pack lunch 3 days a week (buy it the other 2, guilt-free), with a drawn packed lunchbox. Slide 3: One year of workday lunches, $15 bought, $4 packed, 48 work weeks: buy all 5 days $3,600; pack 3, buy 2 $2,016; you keep $1,584 (every year).

Littlefold 3-slide carousel. Slide 1: '3 am Club · No. 2' badge, '3 am, and baby wants to play?' in a large serif with highlighted words, a halftone baby shoe, and the handwritten note 'new night tip every Mon · Wed · Fri'. Slide 2: Keep 3 am boring (low light, quiet voice, no play), with a drawn dim bedside lamp. Slide 3: Fed? Changed? Straight back down (and make days bright, so they learn night from day), with a drawn crib. Source: NHS.

Locked Hour 3-slide carousel. Slide 1: black label 'One Word · No. 3', 'Third coffee not working?' and the huge word 'Nap.' over a pink highlighter stripe, a halftone coffee cup, and the note '10 minutes asleep, alarm on'. Slide 2: '10 minutes. That's it.' A clock ring filled to 10 minutes; 'Then get up. No snooze.' and '30 minutes? you wake up groggy.' Slide 3: 'Sharper right away.' In a sleep lab, a 10-minute nap made adults short on sleep more alert right away. Do this: set a 15-minute alarm: about 5 to drift off, 10 asleep. Source: Brooks & Lack 2006.

Hourback 3-slide carousel. Slide 1: 'AI, for real · Day 9' badge, 'He wants $500. Again.' in a large serif with highlighted words, black-and-white chat bubbles, and the handwritten note 'new one every Mon · Wed · Fri'. Slide 2: Ask AI: 'Help me say no to lending $500.' Add: kind, firm, no excuses (those 3 words set the tone). Slide 3: 'It wrote:' and a chat bubble with the AI's reply, word for word: 'Hey, I'm going to say no to lending the $500. I care about you and I want to keep money from getting between us, so I'm not lending right now. I hope you find a way to sort it out.' Note: real AI reply, situation made up for this post.
